verdict.rationale: Entra's Lifecycle Workflows are first-party governance automation. They manage users across three lifecycle phases and run processes automatically as users move through them, and Entra provisioning pushes users into SaaS and on-prem apps. The evidence does not name the hire, role-change and departure triggers, does not show the workflows are no-code, and does not show how workflows drive per-app actions. missing for 10: explicit joiner/mover/leaver trigger documentation, evidence of a no-code workflow builder, documented linkage between workflows and app-by-app provisioning/deprovisioning, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, identity events trigger automation — no-code workflows on hire, role change, and departure handle the app-by-app choreography for me

citations.quote: Lifecycle workflows (LCW) are identity governance capabilities that enable organizations to manage Microsoft Entra users across the three phases of a user's lifecycle with an organization
Workflows contain specific processes that run automatically against users as they move through their lifecycle.
Common scenarios include provisioning a Microsoft Entra user into SaaS applications like Dropbox, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and many more.
Microsoft Entra ID also supports provisioning users into applications hosted on-premises or in a virtual machine, without having to open up any firewalls.
